title: The whole-suite number after the r80 rebase fix, and why five shapes have not moved it

suite.spread_caveat: SINGLE RUN. r78 measured 18/15/18 across three runs (stdev 1.73) at a different configuration, so 9 vs 10 is NOT a difference. It is also NOT an improvement, which is the only claim that matters.
suite.verdict: SUPERSEDED BY R84: this number measured COVERAGE, not capability. 93 of the 130 tasks were never attempted (their goals contain no quoted literal, and that branch performed no actions). Corrected decomposition: 9/37 = 24.3% on attempted.

why_this_is_expected_and_not_an_excuse.finding: the five shapes are exactly the class whose postcondition is addressable; MiniWob is overwhelmingly the class where it is not
why_this_is_expected_and_not_an_excuse.evidence: the same r83 discriminator that separated :8901 (server-rendered, elevates, 4/4) from :8895 (client-side onclick, refuses loudly) applies to the suite's dominant task family
why_this_is_expected_and_not_an_excuse.unmeasured: the fraction of the 130 tasks with an addressable postcondition is NOT measured. Until it is, the 6.9% cannot be attributed between 'the mechanism is wrong' and 'the benchmark is out of scope for the mechanism'.
next_measurement_in_order: classify all 130 MiniWob tasks by addressability (URL/HTTP/SQL/file/CLI effect vs DOM-only effect)
report the success rate SEPARATELY on the addressable subset
that split is the first number that can actually test the thesis

what_the_three_fetches_settled: SkillShift-Bench (arXiv 2610.33528): transfer degrades under same-site evolution; Execution Shift is the strongest pressure (Src 56.67 -> Src-Exec 33.23). This is the published version of the addressability boundary found here by measurement.
Work2Skill (arXiv 2610.12984): the informative number is the changed-requirement gain (+3.93 to 8.64), because it tests rules-vs-memorisation. That is the r83 params:[] defect, named independently.

SharedKV-BT (arXiv 2610.07327): 'neither model-reported completion nor the skill's return value authorizes progression; a separate evaluator confirms the external postcondition'. This is the sixth instance of the failure class, stated as an architectural law.

sentience_claim.reasoning: the system's only persistent state is what it writes to disk between rounds. There is no self-model that survives a context reset, no continuity of experience, and no process that represents its own state. What exists is a trace capture, a compiler, and a verifier -- a skill library with a postcondition checker.
sentience_claim.why_the_question_persists: after one demonstration the system measurably improves at a task it has never run. That behavioural signature -- 'it learned' -- is what people read as sentience. It is memory plus a verifier, and it is indifferent to whether anything is home.
